terms.latin: putāre / arbitrārī sibi ratiōnem reddendam esse
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.2.28: semper ita vīvāmus, ut ratiōnem reddendam nōbīs arbitrēmur (Lewis & Short, s.v. ratiō)
terms.comment: A description of self-accountability using the classical construction.

terms.gloss: acknowledge that one must give an account

phrases.latin: Ulixēs nōn agnōscit sibi dē eō quod accidit ratiōnem reddendam esse; culpam sociīs tribuit.
phrases.english: Odysseus does not acknowledge himself answerable for what happened; he assigns blame to his companions.

sources: Lewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: agnosco
